name: Radio Browser
description: Discover radio stations and stream URLs by country, language, and genre.
note: Send a descriptive User-Agent from your server. Discover and rotate available mirrors in production rather than relying on one host. Check stream status and HTTPS support; a listing is not a license to rebroadcast audio.
use: Build a Bulgarian radio station directory or a player filtered by country, language, and genre. Use url_resolved for playback and handle unavailable streams.

name: Open-Meteo
description: Global weather forecasts, historical conditions, and climate data.
note: The hosted free service is for noncommercial use, with a 10,000-call daily limit and additional limits. Commercial use requires a paid plan.
use: Build a personal weather dashboard with current temperatures for your favorite cities.

name: Frankfurter
description: Currency exchange rates from institutional sources, without a signup.
note: Reference rates are not live trading quotes. The v2 API supports provider filtering; cache results rather than repeatedly requesting the same rates.
use: Add a reference currency converter to a travel budget or expense tracker.

name: JSONPlaceholder
description: Fake posts, users, comments, and todos for testing your next app.
note: Write operations are simulated. Changes are not saved to a real database, so this is suitable for demos and tests.
use: Practice fetching a post, displaying a loading state, and handling request errors.

name: PokéAPI
description: A detailed Pokémon database with moves, abilities, and game data.
note: Cache resources and follow the fair-use policy. Access to this community API does not grant rights to Pokémon trademarks or artwork.
use: Build a searchable Pokédex and practice combining related API resources.

name: REST Countries
description: Country names, capitals, currencies, flags, and geographic reference data.
note: The current v5 API requires a key. Older unauthenticated v3.1 examples are deprecated. Check the provider’s current free-plan quota.
use: Populate a country reference panel with capitals, currencies, and language information.

name: Open Library
description: Search books, authors, and editions from an open library catalog.
note: Intended for low-volume, human-facing book discovery. Cache requests; the default limit is 1 request/second. Not intended as a high-traffic commercial backend.
use: Make a reading-list search that helps a person choose a book by title or author.

name: DummyJSON
description: Realistic placeholder products, carts, users, and recipes for prototypes.
note: Public resources need no key; authentication endpoints are separate. Mutations are simulated rather than permanently stored.
use: Prototype a product grid with pagination and a working category filter.

name: TVmaze
description: TV shows, episodes, cast information, and broadcast schedules.
note: The public API is separate from the premium user API. Follow attribution, share-alike licensing, and provider rate limits.
use: Create a show finder that links from a search result to its episode guide.

name: Rick and Morty API
description: Characters, locations, and episodes from the animated series.
note: Use pagination for lists. This fan project is not a license to reuse the underlying television property commercially.
use: Practice filtering and pagination with a character explorer.

name: Dog CEO
description: Random dog photos and breed-based image collections.
note: The API returns image URLs. Check photo rights and attribution before reusing images in a commercial product.
use: Build a small random-photo app and practice asynchronous image loading.

name: TheMealDB
description: Meal recipes, ingredients, and cooking instructions to explore.
note: The shared test key 1 is for development and education. Public app-store releases require supporter access; premium filters need an upgrade.
use: Prototype a recipe search by name and display the returned ingredient list.

name: TheCocktailDB
description: Cocktail recipes searchable by name, ingredient, and drink type.
note: The shared key 1 is a development/education test key. Public app-store releases need a production key; some endpoints are premium.
use: Create a recipe-discovery prototype with ingredient and glass information.

name: Art Institute of Chicago
description: Artwork metadata from the Art Institute’s public collection API.
note: Check each artwork’s public-domain status and image restrictions. API access does not mean every image is unrestricted.
use: Build an art explorer that shows titles, artists, dates, and source links.

name: The Met Collection
description: Museum departments and collection records from The Metropolitan Museum of Art.
note: Open Access images are identified by public-domain status. Confirm the record’s rights before displaying or distributing its images.
use: Start with a department chooser, then let visitors explore collection objects.

name: World Bank
description: Country-level economic and development indicators for data projects.
note: Indicators have different update schedules, coverage, and source notes. Use returned dates and metadata rather than treating every observation as current.
use: Explore Bulgaria’s population history in a chart with year labels and source attribution.

name: NASA Open APIs
description: Space imagery and astronomy data for educational applications.
note: DEMO_KEY is for limited exploration; register for your own key for regular use. APOD can include third-party copyrighted media.
use: Create an astronomy-of-the-day viewer that retains the media credit.

name: USGS Earthquakes
description: Earthquake locations, magnitudes, and times in GeoJSON.
note: Use the real-time feeds for regularly refreshed displays when possible. This directory is not an emergency alerting service.
use: Plot recent seismic events on a map with magnitude and observation time.

name: WeatherAPI.com
description: Current conditions and forecast data with location lookup.
note: Register for a key. Free access has plan-specific quotas and feature limits; confirm the current pricing and attribution terms before launch.
use: Add a current-weather panel to a city guide using a server-side request.

name: Alpha Vantage
description: Financial time series and market data for research applications.
note: The standard free allowance is 25 calls/day. Premium datasets and real-time market data can require payment and additional entitlements.
use: Practice charting historical daily prices with appropriate date and source labels.

name: NewsAPI
description: Search news articles and headlines for a development prototype.
note: The free Developer plan is development-only, with 100 requests/day and delayed articles. Staging and production require a paid subscription.
use: Prototype a headline reader with source links; the API does not provide full article text.

name: iTunes Search
description: Search podcast, music, and audiobook catalog metadata from Apple.
note: Apple’s archived documentation describes approximately 20 calls/minute, subject to change. Cache searches and follow promotional-content terms; search access does not grant rights to reuse audio or artwork.
use: Create a podcast discovery directory with links to each show’s publisher or store page.

name: Open Trivia DB
description: Trivia questions with categories, difficulty levels, and multiple-choice answers.
note: Follow the documented request interval and CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution requirements. Responses may contain HTML entities; decode them safely as text. Session tokens can reduce repeat questions.
use: Build a themed quiz with a difficulty selector and explanations for the final score.

name: Nager.Date
description: Public holiday dates and local names for country-specific calendars.
note: The public REST API and offline packages have different access conditions. Offline Docker and NuGet options require a license key. Verify regional coverage and observed-day rules before using dates in business scheduling.
use: Add Bulgarian public holidays to a travel planner or team calendar.

name: ipify
description: Retrieve the public IP address seen by a small JSON endpoint.
note: This endpoint reports the requester’s public IPv4 address, not their location. Server-side calls return the server’s address; IPv6 and dual-stack endpoints are documented separately.
use: Build a network diagnostics page that shows the connection’s public address.

name: Random User
description: Generate sample user profiles for interface demos and test fixtures.
note: Use the seed parameter for repeatable examples and a versioned endpoint when stability matters. These profiles are test data, not genuine customers or testimonials.
use: Prototype a contact list with repeatable sample profiles, sorting, and pagination.

name: Datamuse
description: Find rhymes, related words, spelling matches, and autocomplete suggestions.
note: No key is needed until 1 January 2027, when the provider says API keys will become mandatory. The documented allowance is 100,000 requests/day. Credit Datamuse in public apps and contact the provider for customer-facing use.
use: Build a rhyme finder or a word-game helper with meaning and spelling filters.

name: Open Food Facts
description: Barcode-based food product information, ingredients, and nutrition data.
note: Public reads require an identifying User-Agent; writes need authentication. Follow endpoint rate limits, attribution, and share-alike conditions. Data is community-contributed and may be incomplete. Use staging for testing.
use: Build a barcode product lookup showing available ingredients, source links, and missing-data states.

name: GBIF
description: Biodiversity observations and species records from contributing datasets.
note: Most public reads do not require authentication; downloads and some operations do. Follow dataset licenses and attribution, identify your app, and handle HTTP 429. Use bulk downloads for large retrievals.
use: Create a biodiversity explorer with Bulgarian observation locations, dates, and dataset credits.

name: Crossref
description: Find scholarly metadata, DOI records, publication dates, and journal information.
note: No signup is needed for public metadata reads. Identify your app and use the polite pool for regular requests. Metadata completeness varies; abstracts may be copyrighted, and records do not imply access to full papers.
use: Create a research bibliography finder that links speech-synthesis papers to their DOIs.

name: Sunrise-Sunset.org
description: Sunrise, sunset, twilight, and day-length calculations for coordinates.
note: Attribute Sunrise-Sunset.org as requested by the provider. Parse the returned timezone information carefully; default results are in UTC. This service provides solar times, not cloud cover or weather forecasts.
use: Add daylight times for Sofia to a photography or outdoor-trip planner.

name: PoetryDB
description: Search poems by author, title, line content, or poem length.
note: The service returns poems as structured text. Preserve author attribution, check rights for the intended use, and handle missing matches rather than assuming every request returns a poem.
use: Create a poem-of-the-day reader or a literature search tool for students.
